narrative_summary: The current political and institutional landscape is defined by profound institutional friction, as a resurgent Democratic legislative majority clashes with an increasingly defiant and cornered executive branch. Amid historic turnover in Congress and plunging approval ratings for President Trump following midterm defeats, the administration is aggressively consolidating power through sweeping personnel purges and restrictive congressional oversight directives. Concurrently, systemic vulnerabilities are multiplying across multiple sectors, highlighted by widespread technological disruptions, critical cybersecurity breaches, and escalating geopolitical and nuclear tensions involving Iran and Russia. Economic anxieties and market corrections in the artificial intelligence sector further compound these domestic strains, intensifying debates over governance, corporate accountability, and the erosion of democratic norms.

source_summaries.title: Josh Barro: It’s Not Helping that Idiots Are in Charge
bullets: Recent tech outages have caused concern among prominent media figures and Senate Republicans regarding the qualifications of current administration officials.
Vice President-elect JD Vance has attempted to blame prior administrations for ongoing issues despite Donald Trump's previous presidency.
Josh Barro joined Tim Miller on The Bulwark podcast to discuss political developments, elections, and administration criticisms.

source_summaries.title: BREAKING: Markwayne Mullin Grilled Over FAA Chaos, ICE Deaths and Football Game Flight
bullets: Markwayne Mullin faced congressional questioning regarding a controversial football game trip, an FAA failure, and deaths in ICE custody.
Commentators Andrew Egger and Will Saletan analyzed Mullin's unsatisfactory responses alongside Kash Patel's refusal to testify.
The discussions highlighted a growing defiance within the administration following the Republican midterm defeat.

source_summaries.title: Our Next Bulwark Founders Town Hall Is December 9
bullets: The Bulwark is hosting its second Founders Town Hall for 2026 on Wednesday, December 9 at 8:30 p.m. EST.
Sarah and JVL will lead the live event to share upcoming plans and answer questions from founding members and Best Friends.
Founding members also have access to an exclusive Founders Lounge on Substack Chat and can gift extra subscription seats to others.

source_summaries.title: WTF Is Happening? No, Seriously, WTF!
bullets: A rapid succession of major technological disruptions recently affected Microsoft, the FAA, banks, Apple services, United Airlines, and the NSA.
The Trump administration and expert consensus attribute these widespread failures to unrelated coincidences rather than malicious cyberattacks.
Skeptics argue that the government lacks definitive proof of innocence, while noting potential risks from sophisticated foreign adversaries and advanced AI capabilities.

source_summaries.title: How Worried Should We Be About a Dirty Bomb? | Command Post
bullets: Lt. Gen. Mark Hertling discussed reports that Iran is considering a dirty bomb attack in Washington and how Donald Trump's potential response could benefit Tehran.
Hertling analyzed how Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping might exploit Trump's upcoming summit and criticized a Pentagon official for opposing Ukraine's strikes inside Russia.
The discussion also covered testimony from Navy chief Hung Cao regarding deteriorating conditions aboard U.S. warships.

source_summaries.title: Beating Trump’s Marxism Will Take FDR-Style Populism
bullets: Recent Democratic Senate victories, including Mary Peltola's win in Alaska, signal a rising wave of economic populism focused on combating corporate greed.
Addressing severe wealth and power imbalances requires an intelligent form of economic populism to preserve democratic capitalism.
The defense of disgraced Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang by fellow tech billionaires highlights a resistance to corporate oversight and accountability.

source_summaries.title: Trump’s Tough-on-China Talk Was Always Just an Act
bullets: Donald Trump's aggressive rhetoric regarding China was a political selling point rather than a reflection of genuine hawkish policy.
Trump's administration reversed heavy tariffs after China retaliated with export limits on rare earth minerals.
Trump lacks traditional foreign policy convictions and prioritizes personal interests over strategic national concerns.

source_summaries.title: Putin and the Two Stooges’ Fake Negotiations
bullets: A trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, brings together Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping.
A Ukrainian drone and missile attack caused a section of the strategically and symbolically important Kerch Bridge to collapse.
During recent U.S.-backed negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Russian representatives advanced expansive demands regarding European security and Ukraine.

source_summaries.title: What does it mean to be “laser-focused on affordability”?
bullets: Democrats have embraced the slogan of being laser-focused on affordability, but the phrase papers over fundamental policy disagreements.
Political slogans intentionally rely on ambiguity to appeal to voters while masking conflicting technical agendas.
An economic definition of affordability focuses on real income rather than just the nominal price of goods.

source_summaries.title: The AI Buildout Just Hit A Wall
bullets: Ed Elson and Dan Chiolan discuss the future of AI data centers following the midterm elections.
The analysis questions whether data center expansion has reached a dead end or if Big Tech will bypass current moratoriums.

source_summaries.title: NEW TIME: Ed & Aswath Live
bullets: Scott Galloway announced that today's scheduled livestream was delayed due to an unexpected FAA-related issue.
Ed Elson and Professor Damodaran will host the rescheduled livestream today at 5 p.m. ET.
Prof G+ members will have on-demand access to the livestream replay if they miss the live broadcast.

source_summaries.title: Hanging In The Balance
bullets: Nvidia's earnings and CEO Jensen Huang's role are the focus of a live earnings review hosted with NYU valuation expert Aswath Damodaran.
The upcoming Anthropic IPO is highlighted as a much more significant indicator for the future of the AI market than Nvidia's current performance.
The Extra Credit newsletter is shifting to a weekly schedule, featuring deep-dive business stories and a new interview series hosted by Ed Elson.

source_summaries.title: Nvidia Is Better Off Without Jensen Huang
bullets: Ed Elson and Gil Luria analyze Nvidia's first earnings report following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang.
The discussion covers potential shareholder-friendly CEO successors and evaluates the current state of the artificial intelligence bubble.
Sherri Davidoff reviews recent technology outages and their underlying causes, while Ed Elson shares perspective on Anthropic's IPO.

source_summaries.title: America Is Running Out of Young People – with Lyman Stone
bullets: Falling U.S. birth rates are primarily driven by fewer people marrying and pairing off.
Financial incentives and immigration alone will not close the demographic gap.
Safety net marriage penalties discourage working-class couples from getting married, while a shrinking pool of 18-year-olds threatens American colleges.

source_summaries.title: A Fabulous Debt.
bullets: Financial Times Alphaville editor Robin Wigglesworth was featured as a guest on Episode 33 of the News Items Podcast.
Wigglesworth discussed his new book titled A Fabulous Debt, which explores the history of how bonds built the modern global economy.
The episode highlights how debt instruments have historically financed major historical epochs and continue to underwrite the artificial intelligence revolution.

source_summaries.title: The Beating Heart.
bullets: A cybersecurity start-up used an A.I. model to discover a critical software bug in Java, impacting government agencies and major companies.
Researchers found malicious JavaScript code injected into Optimizely software, affecting approximately 178 organizations before being fixed.
The NSA's classified internal communications network experienced an offline outage, though officials reported no signs of a cyberattack.

source_summaries.title: They Were Just Admitted to the Bar. Now They’re Federal Prosecutors. Meet Trump’s New DOJ.
bullets: The Justice Department under President Donald Trump's second administration has fast-tracked numerous inexperienced attorneys, including recent law school graduates, into assistant U.S. attorney positions.
This influx of inexperienced hires comes as thousands of years of combined experience have been lost due to the departure or purging of seasoned career prosecutors.
Legal experts note that hiring attorneys with less than three years of experience for these vital roles is a significant and unprecedented break from past DOJ practice.

source_summaries.title: The Supreme Court before it stood apart
bullets: Rachel A. Shelden's new book, The Political Supreme Court, examines how the 19th-century court and public perception differed greatly from today's apolitical ideal.
Nineteenth-century justices engaged in 'judicial representation' by riding circuit and maintaining regular contact with local communities in their assigned regions.
Early justices like John Marshall and William Johnson actively participated in political discourse, newspaper writing, and public debates.

source_summaries.title: An election impact on the Supreme Court’s immigration docket
bullets: The Supreme Court is considering whether to hear a case regarding the constitutionality of Iowa's 2024 immigration law, Senate File 2340.
Iowa's law criminalizes certain immigration conduct and allows state judges to order defendants to leave the United States.
Lower federal courts previously ruled that the state law is preempted by federal immigration authority and blocked its enforcement.

source_summaries.title: All eyes on the justices’ next private conference
bullets: The Supreme Court announced that several notable petitions will be considered at the justices' upcoming private conference on December 4.
The pending disputes include challenges regarding the Trump administration's ban on transgender servicemembers and the appointment of acting U.S. attorneys.
The Court's next argument session is scheduled to begin on Monday, November 30.

source_summaries.title: Principles for an International Monetary and Financial Commons
bullets: The international financial system functions as a commons prone to degradation and the tragedy of the commons without proper maintenance.
The historical Bretton Woods rules-based order ultimately failed because it could not accommodate large trade flows, capital movements, or U.S. inflation.
The subsequent shift to floating exchange rates introduced significant real relative price volatility that harms businesses, as exchange rates remain unpredictable.

source_summaries.source: Phillips P. OBrien and Ben Hodges from Phillips’s
source_summaries.title: Live with Phillips P. OBrien and Ben Hodges
bullets: Phillips P. OBrien and Ben Hodges hosted a live video discussion lasting thirty minutes.
A recording of the live session was published on November 18, 2026.

source_summaries.title: Now We Act: With Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi on the Strength of Democracy
bullets: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi emphasizes that Democrats must ban corrupt practices like stock trading for everyone, including themselves, while addressing both democracy and prosperity.
The discussion highlighted the necessity for public officials to make a basic choice between making money and serving the public.
Participants addressed the authority of Congress and the importance of rolling back emergency powers that allow the executive branch to bypass constitutional limits.

source_summaries.title: Poll: Trump hits a new low; Americans split on impeachment, favor bills to reduce costs and corruption
bullets: President Trump's approval rating dropped to a new low of 31% following the Democratic midterm victory.
A majority of Americans want the new Congress to prioritize lowering prices and conducting administrative oversight.
The public is evenly split on whether the House should impeach the president, but favors removal by a 51% to 39% margin if impeachment occurs.

source_summaries.title: Schumer or Van Hollen?
bullets: Senate Democrats will choose between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for their next Majority Leader on December 1.
The upcoming leadership vote will serve as an important signal for the future direction of the Democratic Party.
The decision involves participating incumbent and newly elected senators, excluding those retiring or replaced.

source_summaries.title: Sabato's Crystal Ball - Virginia 2026: Even Bluer than 2025 - Vol. 24, Iss. 88
bullets: Virginia Democrats followed up on their strong 2025 performance with another very blue election in 2026.
Senator Mark Warner secured reelection by a wide margin, and Democrats successfully flipped two U.S. House seats.
Republicans managed to retain the 5th District due to a continuing reddening trend in Southside Virginia.

source_summaries.title: Generation Swing
bullets: Historically, voters under 30 voted similarly to older demographics until a noticeable generational gap began to emerge in the 1990s and 2000s.
Following decades of strong alignment with the Democratic Party, young voters experienced a notable 17-point shift to the right in the 2024 election.
Young men specifically moved from supporting Joe Biden by nine points in 2020 to supporting Donald Trump by 14 points in 2024.

source_summaries.title: Where Did Iran’s Bomb Fuel Go? — What the Satellite Photos Show
bullets: The IAEA issued a warning that it has lost track of 440 kilograms of near bomb-grade uranium in Iran and cannot locate its newest enrichment plant.
Satellite imagery from June 2025 indicates trucks may have removed enriched uranium from the Fordow site shortly before American airstrikes.
Recent satellite photos show ongoing excavation and vehicle activity at the Isfahan tunnel complex, where the missing nuclear material is believed to be relocated.

source_summaries.title: Now We Act: With Rep. Jamie Raskin on the Constitution vs. Corruption
bullets: Timothy Snyder features Representative Jamie Raskin in an unscripted conversation for the Now We Act series.
Raskin is highlighted as the presumptive chair of the House Judiciary Committee.
The discussion focuses on upholding the Constitution against corruption and tyranny.

source_summaries.source: Prof Robert Pape from Escalation Trap
source_summaries.title: All Three Iran Warning Signs Now Flashing — RED
bullets: Prof Robert Pape warns that all three escalation warning signs regarding Iran have flashed red within a two-week period.
Washington is currently discussing the threat of a dirty bomb in relation to Iran.
President Trump recently stated that Iran would face unprecedented consequences.

source_summaries.title: In Defense of Sarah Longwell. Against One-Party Democracy.
bullets: Garry Kasparov defends Sarah Longwell against critics who accused her of abandoning conservative principles by aligning with Democrats.
Kasparov argues that principled conservatives have naturally aligned with Democrats because the Republican Party under Donald Trump has become authoritarian.
The author contends that American democracy suffers because the Democratic Party is currently the only major political option operating from a baseline of free and fair elections.

source_summaries.source: Don Moynihan, William Resh, and Gary Hollibaugh from Can We Still Govern?
source_summaries.title: Trauma, Not Dignity
bullets: Federal employee departures driven by the voluntary resignation program were frequently coerced rather than truly voluntary.
The federal workforce experienced a net loss of approximately 280,000 employees between January 2025 and August 2026.
The vast majority of federal workforce reductions occurred through resignations and retirements rather than direct firings.

source_summaries.title: How “wave babies” took over Congress
bullets: At least 109 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives will be held by freshmen in January 2027, marking the largest congressional turnover in decades.
The surge in newcomers is driven by both a Democratic electoral tsunami and a record number of voluntary departures by incumbents.
A record 61 members chose to retire or run for another office rather than seek reelection, led heavily by Republicans seeking to avoid a difficult political environment.

source_summaries.title: Don’t ICEwash or Griftwash the Midterms
bullets: Paul Krugman argues that attributing the Democratic midterm victory solely to affordability ignores the historic scale of the win and other driving factors.
Data and polling analysis suggest that Republican policies on immigration enforcement and widespread corruption significantly damaged the party at the ballot box.
Voter perceptions of issues like cruelty and corruption interacted with economic frustrations rather than existing as isolated concerns.

source_summaries.title: The U.S. lost measles elimination after 26 years. Now what?
bullets: The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status after 26 years due to declining vaccination rates across numerous communities.
More than 28 percent of U.S. counties now fall below the 90 percent MMR vaccination threshold required to maintain herd immunity.
Falling vaccination coverage has led to outbreaks causing preventable illnesses, hospitalizations, and deaths, predominantly affecting unvaccinated children.

source_summaries.title: White House prepares to give Congress the finger
bullets: White House Counsel Will Scharf issued a memo requiring federal agencies to obtain White House approval before testifying before congressional committees.
The directive is a radical departure from established policy and directly conflicts with federal law protecting the right of federal employees to furnish information to Congress.
The administration's move comes as officials prepare to resist congressional oversight following Democrats taking control of the House and Senate.

source_summaries.source: Michael Spencer and Jeff Morhous from AI Supremacy
source_summaries.title: Grok Bot vs Dots: Which is the better personal agent?
bullets: The article compares personal AI agents including Grok Bot and OpenAI's Dots while highlighting major industry events such as Anthropic's upcoming IPO and Nvidia's earnings.
Anthropic is slated to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT as its revenue and product ecosystem rapidly expand.
Nvidia faces stock corrections down 36 percent from its all-time high despite generating significant quarterly revenue compared to leading AI startups.

source_summaries.title: What the last two bubbles tell us about the AI boom
bullets: Wall Street analysts remained overwhelmingly bullish at the peak of the 1990s tech bubble and the onset of the 2008 financial crisis.
Analyst recommendations for current artificial intelligence stocks mirror past market peaks by staying overwhelmingly positive despite accumulating bad news.
The central question surrounding the current AI market boom is whether it will conclude with a sudden crash or a slow deflation.

source_summaries.title: Office Hours: Who Should Be the Next Senate Majority Leader?
bullets: Democrats will hold 56 seats in the Senate next year following the election of Mary Peltola.
Incumbent Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen for the majority leader position.
The secret ballot vote to determine the next Senate majority leader is scheduled for December 1.
